reason: The narrative centers on David (דָוִד), introduced as a young shepherd boy (רֹעֶה - 'ro'eh') tending his father Jesse's flocks. Though narrated in third person, the story consistently follows David's experiences and perspective: his father sending him to the battlefield with provisions, his shock at Goliath's challenge, his direct engagement with the central conflict, and his ultimate victory. The text explicitly emphasizes David's humble, non-elite status as a young, inexperienced shepherd ('נַעַר' - 'na'ar', a youth/boy; 'רֹעֶה' - a shepherd/working person) in contrast to the armored professional soldiers. The narrative values David's perspective and agency despite—and indeed, because of—his ordinary working-class background, establishing him as the heroic protagonist.
